comments.body: `containsAny` is matched with `.every(...)`, so the client requires every selected option to be present. The server has the opposite meaning: `computeWhereConditionParts` maps `containsAny` to `"key"::text[] && ARRAY[...]::text[]` (array overlap, i.e. any), and `computeViewRecordGqlOperationFilter.ts:623` sends the selected options as `containsAny`. Example: a MULTI_SELECT view filter Contains [A, B] and a record with value ['A']. The server returns the record. Here `['A','B'].every(i => ['A'].includes(i))` is false, so `isRecordMatchingFilter` (`isRecordMatchingFilter.ts:186`) says the record does not match. `triggerUpdateRecordOptimisticEffect.ts:68` then drops the record from the cached edges of that filtered query, and `triggerCreateRecordsOptimisticEffect.ts:90` will not add a newly created record with a partial match. The list is wrong until the next refetch. The fix is `.some(...)` in place of `.every(...)`.
